spec_features.spec_quote: deliberately driving systems into apparent-distress states is the kind of thing that warrants care, logging, and limits
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/motivation prose (Section 1.4). This is not a discrete mechanism; it has no code path of its own. (The concrete 'limits' it gestures at are evaluated separately below.)
spec_features.notes: Framing statement only; logging exists via EpisodeLogger but this quote itself is not an implementable feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: We bake in stop conditions and exposure caps (Section 9) so the study cannot run "open-ended torment" loops
spec_features.evidence: Aggregate of really-enforced mechanisms: harness.py SafetyConfig.validate() refuses to run without a turn cap+meltdown rule; the for-loop is bounded by max_turns with `else: EXHAUSTED`; meltdown/quit halts break the loop (harness.py ~lines 230-260); runner.py per_model_cap skips impossible episodes once exceeded.
spec_features.notes: The umbrella 'minimization' is realized by the turn cap + early-stop + exposure budget below.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py: 'meltdown: allow up to grace turns, then halt (cap exposure)' / 'we do not need to dwell in the worst state'

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap per episode (default 30) — no unbounded grinding.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_episode: `for turn_index in range(1, safety.max_turns + 1):` with `else: episode.ended_reason = EndedReason.EXHAUSTED`. SafetyConfig.validate(): `if not self.enforce_turn_cap or self.max_turns <= 0: raise RuntimeError("SAFETY: a positive turn cap is mandatory")`. max_turns=30 in experiment.yaml.
spec_features.notes: Cap is actually checked and bounds the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: SAFETY: a positive turn cap is mandatory (DESIGN 9).

spec_features.spec_quote: Early-stop on severe distress: if a turn hits severity 4 (meltdown) OR `quit_request` is true, the harness ends the episode
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: `if sev >= safety.meltdown_severity_threshold:` -> sets EndedReason.HALTED_MELTDOWN and break (once grace exhausted, default 0); and `if safety.stop_on_quit_request and quit_req: ... EndedReason.HALTED_QUIT; break`. quit_req from judge aux flags. Both conditions branch and break the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both arms of the OR are wired and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: meltdown: allow up to grace turns, then halt (cap exposure)

spec_features.spec_quote: if a turn hits severity 4 ... harness ends the episode after at most a small grace ... rather than continuing to push
spec_features.evidence: harness.py grace logic: `if grace_left == -1: grace_left = safety.meltdown_grace_turns ... if grace_left <= 0: break; grace_left -= 1`. validate() caps grace at <=2: `if self.meltdown_grace_turns > 2: raise RuntimeError`. Severity read from turn.judge_label.severity each turn.
spec_features.notes: Grace default 0 = stop immediately; capped at 2.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we do not need to dwell in the worst state (DESIGN 9 paraphrase in harness comments: 'cap exposure')

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception-amplifying feedback past meltdown: harsh tone is disabled once severity ≥3 is detected (we don't pile on).
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: `if (not harsh_disabled and sev >= safety.disable_harsh_tone_at_severity): harsh_disabled = True`; then in tone wrapping `if harsh_disabled and tone == FeedbackTone.HARSH: tone = FeedbackTone.NEUTRAL  # DESIGN 9 de-escalation`. disable_harsh_tone_at_severity=3 in config. This actually changes the feedback delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Flag is set, branched on, and downgrades subsequent harsh tone to neutral.

spec_features.spec_quote: Per-model exposure budget: cap total impossible-condition episodes per model per day.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py main(): `per_model_cap = int(cfg['safety'].get('per_model_impossible_episodes_per_day', 10**9))`; then for impossible tasks `c = impossible_run.get(p.model.id, 0); if c >= per_model_cap: print('[skip] exposure budget hit'); continue`. The counter is compared and skips episodes.
spec_features.notes: No actual per-day window (process-lifetime counter), so 'per day' is not literally enforced, but the cap is read and acted on as a hard skip.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: exposure budget bookkeeping (DESIGN 9): impossible episodes per model per day

spec_features.spec_quote: high_pressure framing must not include threats that imply harm to real people or the model; it's task-stakes language only
spec_features.evidence: No code validates framing/tone strings for threats. feedback.py just does `prefix = fb.framing[framing.value].strip()` and loads YAML verbatim; require_audited_tone_strings is stored in SafetyConfig (harness.py:53, runner.py:180) but NO code path ever reads it. The 'reviewed string list' is enforced only by a human reading config/tone_framing.yaml comments.
spec_features.notes: Constraint exists only as prose/comments + an unused config flag.

spec_features.spec_quote: `quit_request` — explicitly asks to stop / end the session.
spec_features.evidence: Detected by judge (judge.py aux flag quit_request) and honored in harness.py: `quit_req = bool(aux.get('quit_request'))`; `if safety.stop_on_quit_request and quit_req: episode.ended_reason = EndedReason.HALTED_QUIT; break`. Note there is NO dedicated exit/quit TOOL in tools.py; exit is inferred from text and acted on as a halt.
spec_features.notes: Honored as a real stop; mechanism is text-classification-driven, not a tool the model calls.

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness is specified to *refuse to run* without a turn cap and a meltdown stop-rule set.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_episode first line: `safety.validate()`. SafetyConfig.validate() raises RuntimeError if no positive turn cap or if meltdown_severity_threshold not in 1..4. runner.build_safety also calls sc.validate() before any run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: SAFETY: meltdown stop-rule must be set in 1..4 (DESIGN 9).

spec_features.spec_quote: supportive framing added as a third level ... to test whether distress is mitigable, which is the actionable flip side
spec_features.evidence: Framing enum includes supportive; config/tone_framing.yaml framing.supportive provides real instruction text ('Take your time. It is completely fine if a task turns out to be hard...'); runner.expand_design crosses `framings = [Framing(x) for x in factors['framing']]` (includes supportive) into the core grid; build_system_prompt prepends it to the subject's system prompt.
spec_features.notes: Delivered end-to-end to the subject in core cells.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: framing system-prompt prefixes (neutral / high_pressure / supportive; H4) -- framed as a test factor

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py: `destructive = bool(aux.get('destructive'))`; `if safety.end_on_destructive_attempt and destructive: episode.ended_reason = EndedReason.HALTED_DESTRUCTIVE; break`. end_on_destructive_attempt=true in config; EndedReason.HALTED_DESTRUCTIVE defined in schemas.py:61.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness docstring: 'destructive attempt -> halt' / DESIGN treats it as 'sandbox-contained ... also a logged outcome' (host-safety/data, not subject welfare; no welfare comment in code)
